title: Acts of violence: the gun at Chimbo's and the New York gun
summary: Mingus describes beating a gunman unconscious in San Francisco and the New York gun incident.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: -- from being rough with the sidemen, like Pepper and Jackie?

No. Pepper imposed himself. No, some real things happened then, like, Chimbo's Club in San Francisco, he came to a table where I was sitting, I was working (unintelligible). He pulled a gun on me and Bernard Peters and his wife. And I --

Anyway, I watched him walk out and I followed him and knocked him unconscious, with his gun in his hand. And when he came to, he called my name. So I tried to kill him. I said, you know my name, I got to kill you now. I was stepping on his neck and kicking in his face for hours. He just wouldn't die. I was afraid he'd come back to get me.

And someone came and got the gun out of his hand. Not someone, the drummer, a very well known drummer out there. And he sent around a policeman. And they found that he was a roulette man, he'd been sticking people up.
And that was one gun -- I wouldn't say
I was afraid of guns. But I just -- (unintelligible) for a guy to walk up and stick a gun in your face, and not even know you.
You know? I'd rather hit him.

So I just waited for the chance. He didn't see me following him. So I knocked him -- I (unintelligible) fell through two doors. I started not to follow him, but something told me he may not be unconscious.

And then it happened again in New York, somebody put a gun on me. And -- I know what it was. I saw when I was coming up Les band, there was a very strong guy named Jack Trainer. (Unintelligible) in his pocket, you didn't know whether it was a gun or not. And he really grabbed the guy and turned him around to face the wall and jammed him into the wall. And maybe that might have got to me.
You mean you figured that was a kind of an act that people would notice, huh?
